A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CAST study. The full text, equations, Figures 1–5, Tables 1–5, and Appendices A–F are readable and matchable despite pagination changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original inference-speed experiments in Section 5, with batch-size analyses, component ablations, and additional GPU comparisons in Appendices E–F.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark experiments, batch-size analyses, component ablations, and GPU comparisons in Section 5 and Appendices E–F.

M1.justification: CAST's cost lookup tables, breadth and depth pruning, dynamic reranking, and Algorithm 1 are unchanged. No algorithmic component or inference procedure is revised.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same six tasks using MT-bench, HumanEval, GSM8K, Alpaca, CNN/Daily Mail, and Natural Questions. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within the corresponding experiments: Table 1 retains SpD, PLD, Medusa, Lookahead, and the EAGLE variants where applicable. The batching, ablation, batch-size, and GPU comparisons also retain their comparator sets.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendices E–F retain the same model configurations, decoding temperatures, batch sizes, GPU setups, hyperparameters, and speedup-ratio metric. No evaluation protocol or stated setting changes.

E4.justification: The acceptance-length/probability analysis in Figure 3, verified-token sensitivity in Figure 4, batch-size study in Figure 5, and component ablation in Table 3 are unchanged.

E5.justification: The single-run speedup description and Figure 3's fitted relationships are unchanged. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, seed information, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–5 and Figures 3–5 retain identical results, including all appendix experiments. For example, Table 1 still reports a 5.23x CAST speedup for Llama-3.3-70B on HumanEval at batch size 1 and temperature 0.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and derivations in Sections 3–4, Theorem 4.1, and its proof in Appendix D are unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about cost-aware tree construction, generalizing EAGLE-2/EAGLE-3, evaluation across six tasks and six models, and up to 5.2x speedup with typical 5–20% improvements over prior methods.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning accepted-token count versus speedup, batching, model scaling, and component effects are unchanged. Appendix E retains the same limitation concerning precomputation of inference costs.

D1.justification: v2's abstract newly states that code is available and supplies the EAGLE-Research/sglang-eagle4 repository address. v1 lacks a repository address for the proposed implementation. Existing implementation and hardware details are unchanged; repository contents cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list are unchanged, as is the positioning relative to the EAGLE family and prior work on batched speculative decoding.

P1.justification: v2 changes the second affiliation from Tsinghua University to E Fund Management Co., Ltd., adds a code-availability sentence, publication-status text, and funding acknowledgments. The scientific prose and section sequence remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds ruled ICLR 2026 publication headers and reflows the pages, placing the conclusion and acknowledgments on page 10 and shifting subsequent material. Figures and tables retain their designs and captions; changes concern placement, spacing, and pagination.

improvement.justification: The newly supplied implementation repository address modestly improves reproducibility documentation by giving readers a concrete code location absent from v1. The scientific arguments and empirical evidence, including the appendices, remain unchanged. The PDFs alone do not establish the repository's completeness or usability.
